features.text: The patient has a positive lab result for hepatitis C.
The patient has no prior history of hepatitis C.
The patient has a history of intravenous drug use but has been clean for over fifteen years.
The patient consumes alcohol occasionally, having reduced consumption from the past.
The patient smokes approximately one to two cigarettes per day and is trying to quit.
The patient has a family history of hypertension, diabetes, and depression.
The patient has no current medications and is otherwise in good health.
The patient's vital signs are within normal limits.
The patient has a grade two out of six systolic ejection murmur.
The patient has no hepatosplenomegaly, with only splenomegaly noted.
The patient's liver panel shows an elevated AST at thirty-nine, but ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin are within normal limits.
The patient is concerned about the risk of hepatitis C transmission to their family members.
The patient prefers to have their family members screened for hepatitis C and is willing to follow up in three weeks.
